title: Retraction from a w-local map after restricting to a closed component union
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings with w-local spectra [def-weil-pbc-w-local], and let g:R\to S be a ring map. Assume g is bijective on all prime stalks [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and sends every closed point of Spec S to a closed point of Spec R. Let h:\pi_0(\operatorname{Spec}S)\to\pi_0(\operatorname{Spec}R) be the map induced by contraction of primes along g, and let T\subseteq\pi_0(\operatorname{Spec}S) be closed. If the restriction h|_T:T\to\pi_0(\operatorname{Spec}R) is bijective, then there exists a ring map s:S\to R with s\circ g=\mathrm{id}_R.

proof.text: Lift R and S to ULift.{v} R and ULift.{u} S in their common maximum universe, using the canonical ring equivalences eR and eS. Their spectra are homeomorphic to the original spectra and hence have bijective maps cR and cS on connected components. The lifted rings are w-local by transport along the surjective inverse equivalences [def-weil-pbc-w-local]. Equip the lifted S with the algebra structure induced by the lifted map g′ = eS.symm ∘ g ∘ eR; its algebra map is g′.

proof.text: Ring equivalences are bijective on prime stalks, and this property is stable under composition. Thus the stalk bijectivity of g [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] transports to g′, giving the auxiliary theorem’s stalk hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 09AZ, proof of implication (3) to (1), paragraph assuming the local rings are identified

proof.text: The spectrum homeomorphisms preserve closed points, and the comap square commutes, so the closed-point hypothesis transports to g′. Set T′ = cS⁻¹(T); continuity of cS makes T′ closed. The commuting square on components and bijectivity of cR and cS transport the given bijection on T to a bijection on T′. Its surjectivity and injectivity supply precisely the two component hypotheses of the auxiliary theorem.

source.place: Tag 09AZ, proof of implication (3) to (1), paragraph after choosing the closed range T

proof.text: Apply the closed-component retraction theorem [lem-weil-pbc-wlocal-isClosed-bijOn-retraction] to g′ and T′ in the common universe. It yields s′ with s′ ∘ g′ = id. The explicit composite s = eR ∘ s′ ∘ eS.symm satisfies s ∘ g = id by evaluating this identity at ULift.up r and applying ULift.down.

lean.statement: theorem RingHom.exists_retraction_of_closed_component_bijective {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [IsWLocalRing R] [IsWLocalRing S] (g : R →+* S) (hstalk : g.BijectiveOnStalks) (hclosed : ∀ y ∈ closedPoints (PrimeSpectrum S), PrimeSpectrum.comap g y ∈ closedPoints (PrimeSpectrum R)) (T : Set (ConnectedComponents (PrimeSpectrum S))) (hT : IsClosed T) (hbij : Function.Bijective (fun t : T ↦ (PrimeSpectrum.continuous_comap g).connectedComponentsMap t.val)) : ∃ s : S →+* R, s.comp g = RingHom.id R
